newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum tags must fall to compete with steel-Ford.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum tags must fall to compete with steel-Ford.

text.p: A Ford Motor Co executive said Wednesday that the price of aluminum would have to stabilise at lower levels before U.S. automakers would consider dramatically increasing their use of the material in manufacturing vehicles.

William Powers, vice president of research at Ford, told Reuters that the automakers "roughly" agreed with a joint study by the aluminum industry and Energy Department which showed that aluminum prices would have to be about three times the price of steel before the lightweight metal would become cost competitive with other metals used in automaking.
He estimated that aluminum prices were currently four times or more higher than the price of steel.
"At this point in time, I think they still have a little ways to go in stabilising prices and getting a price that we feel is competitive with other material. They need to come down," Powers said.
He was attending Alumitech, an industry forum organised by the U.S. Aluminum Association.

Powers was speaking a day after Alumax Inc CEO Allen Born predicted that the auto industry had been convinced of aluminum's superiority to steel, and predicted that within ten years, half the cars manufactured in North America would be made completely from aluminum.
"That's that's their stretch objective," Powers said when asked to comment on the Alumax executive's prediction.

"To make that come true, we have to see the valid business case. Whenever we do make the big change, there will be a little bit of chicken and egg. We'll both be making a gamble of some sorts," Powers said.
Changing technology would help producers close the price gap with steel, Powers said.
